Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx + throughput drop despite reserved capacity (prod) — initial triage

Team — quick findings from the on-call triage:
- Observed sustained queuing at the pool ingress; token-generation kernel is showing high contention.
- KV cache churn is high for OrbitBank’s prefix distribution (frequent cold starts) — evictions spike when concurrent sessions > 600.
- GPU utilization is at 78%, but queue depth and scheduler latency are driving the p95 increase.

Immediate mitigations I can execute now (low risk):
1) Raise per-route concurrency cap for OrbitBank temporarily to reduce head-of-line blocking (20m change).
2) Enable model-variant fallback (7B-opt) for maintenance window — reduces per-request GPU time ~18%.
3) Increase small burst capacity on the dedicated pool by 5 GPUs (requires exec OK for burst spend).

I attached the kv-cache snapshot and the pooled metrics export. I’ll start with step (1) and report back.

—Aditya
Sr. SRE, Serving Runtime
Attachments: kv-cache-snapshot.txt, pool-metrics-20280724.csv
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 10:02:12 -07:00
Subject: RE: technical mitigation options and risks (OrbitBank)

Follow-up from eng: more context and risk matrix.

Root cause hypothesis: high-frequency prefix churn + long sequences causing the runtime to retain large KV caches while scheduler backpressure increases — results in effective throughput drop even when raw GPU utilization looks moderate. There’s also an observed kernel-path fallback that kicks in when sequence length variance spikes, increasing latency for some requests.

Proposed immediate steps (ordered):
A) Activate per-route aggressive KV prefix caching for OrbitBank (reduce cold-starts) — low risk, 30m to validate.
B) Deploy a short-lived model-variant routing rule to route <=512 token requests to our 7B-opt. This reduces per-token GPU time and should recover throughput quickly — medium risk (quality delta to validate).
C) Authorize a 24–48 GPU-hour burst to add capacity while we run telemetry for 24h — requires exec approval.

Rollback plan included for each step. If we do A+B now I expect to see p95 latency return under 1s for the majority of traffic within 1–2 hours.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Serving Runtime
